work.title: Til begge deres kongel. Majestæters, den stormægtigste Arvekonges og Herres, Friderich den Femtes, den stormægtigste Dronnings, Lovises, fød kongel. Princesse til Storbritannien, høytidelige Salvingsfest, blev følgende Syngedigt opført

history.p: Scheibe composed the present work for the ceremony of anointing of the new royal couple, King Frederik V and Queen Louise; the event took place after the obligatory year of mourning in September 1747. The event was celebrated all over the country with music, pageants and reciting of dedicatory poems, and even the smallest provincial towns were decorated. The text, which Scheibe chose to use for his cantata, is by Lorentz Reerslev who later was to become a famous actor at The Royal Theatre; he also wrote another text which was set to music by the violinist Johann Erasmus Iversen and performed at The Musical Society celebrating the same event. Scheibe's cantata, however, was performed during the official banquet (‘Taffelet’). Only the text book has survived.

incipText.p: Tag nu, velsignede Konge! Din Krone
Med uudsigelig Fornøyelse og Glæde
En sød, en tryg, en stille Roe
Er Du allene Rigets Støtte?
Jeg er min Konges Vogtere
Du Landets Magt, min Støtte, kom
Ja, ja, alt dette er vel værd at prise
Her ere vi Helte, vi os strax tillave

perfResList.head: choir ('De gamle danske og norske Helte')

incipText.p: Et Riges Herlighed vedvarer
Du Nordens Soel skal sildig dale
Bliv ved at tale, viise Mund!
Der, hvor man baade seer og hører
Det skal til Nordens Ære blive
Ja billigen enhver sig fryder
Du Landetsfader! Folkets Lyst!
Men hisset Mildhed staaer og bier
Den mildeste Konge, som findes paa Jorden
At giøre got imod enhver
Jeg staaer som henrykt ved at see
O! mægtige Beskyttere!
Her skal mit Øye altid vaage
O Store Kongepar!

annot.p: No indication as to whether this is an aria or perhaps a recitative; neither is there any indication as to the character(s) singing this section. They are presumably Sikkerhed and Kongernes Skydsengel; cf. other text source.
